questions.question: Little Andaman in the south is separated from the Nicobar Islands by the ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __10° channel__.

• The Ten Degree Channel, which is about **90 miles (145 kilometers)** wide, separates Andaman and Nicobar Islands in the south.
 
• The union territory of India's Andaman and Nicobar Islands is made up of two groups of islands off the coast of the Bay of Bengal.
 
• Between Myanmar (Burma) and the Indonesian island of Sumatra, the peaks of a submerged mountain range, the Andaman Islands, and their southern neighbors, the Nicobar Islands, form an arc extending 620 miles (1,000 km) southward.
 
• The arc marks the western border of the Bay of Bengal and the eastern border of the Andaman Sea. 
 
• Port Blair is the territorial capital (on South Andaman Island).
 
• The islands are home to the Andaman and Nicobar Command, the Indian Armed Forces' only tri-service geographical command.
 
• According to the **2011 Indian Census**, the **Union Territory of Andaman and Nicobar Islands** had a population of **379,944**, with 202,330 men (53.25 percent) and 177,614 women (46.75 percent).
 
• There were 878 females for every 1,000 males. The Nicobar Islands are home to just 10% of the population.

questions.question: Which of the following is the highest hill station in India?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Leh **__is the highest hill station in India.
 
• It has a cold desert climate (Köppen climate classification BWk) with long, cold winters from late November to early March
 
• It is the largest town of the union territory of Ladakh.
 
• **Leh** is at an altitude of** 3,524 m (11,562 ft),** and is connected via National Highway 1 to Srinagar in the southwest and to Manali in the south via the Leh-Manali Highway.
 
• Unlike other districts in India, the Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Council (LAHDC) is in charge of governance in Leh.
 
• Every year Sindhu Darshan Festival is held at Shey, 15 km away from town to promote religious harmony and glory of the Indus (Sindhu) river.
 
• Buddhism is the largest religion in Leh, followed by over 43.8% of people.

questions.question: The peninsular plateau of India was a part of which continent earlier?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Africa**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The peninsular plateau of India was once a part of the ancient supercontinent known as Gondwana.
 
• Gondwana included regions that are now part of Africa, South America, Antarctica, Australia, and the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Over millions of years, the tectonic plates drifted apart, leading to the present-day geographical formations.
 
• This separation and movement of the tectonic plates is explained by the theory of continental drift proposed by Alfred Wegener.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The concept of continental drift was further developed into the theory of plate tectonics, which explains the movement of Earth's lithospheric plates.
 
• India's collision with the Eurasian plate led to the formation of the Himalayas.
 
• The peninsular plateau is characterized by its stable geological structure and is one of the oldest landmasses on Earth.
 
• The plateau is rich in minerals and has significant geological and ecological importance.

questions.question: Why do people living in the Konkan coast NOT encounter extremes of temperature and seasonal rhythm?

options.text: Location on leeward side of Sahyadri

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Coastal Location**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• With a long **coastline**, large coastal areas have an equable climate. 
 
• Areas in the interior of India are far away from the moderating influence of the sea. 
 
• Such areas have extremes of climate.
 
• That is why the people of **Mumbai** and the **Konkan** coast have hardly any idea of extremes of temperature and the seasonal rhythm of weather.
 
• India‘s climate is controlled by a number of factors which can be broadly divided into **two groups** — factors related to location and relief, and factors related to air pressure and winds. 
 
• Factors related to Location and Relief Latitude: the **Tropic of Cancer** passes through the central part of India in an east-west direction. 
 
• Thus, the northern part of India lies in a **sub-tropical **and** temperate zone** and the part lying south of the Tropic of Cancer falls in the tropical zone. 
 
• The tropical zone being **nearer** to the equator experiences high temperatures throughout the year with a small daily and annual range. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Undulating landform** means to have a continuous up and down shape or movement, like waves on the sea.
 
• The **leeward side** is the drier side or the side where the trade winds pass after they hit a mountain.
 
• **Nagpur** lies in interior Maharashtra on the leeward side of the Sahyadri Mountains.
 
• A **monsoon** is a seasonal change in the direction of the prevailing, or strongest, winds of a region.
 
• Monsoons cause wet and dry seasons throughout much of the tropics.
 
• Monsoons are most often associated with the Indian Ocean.
 
• Monsoons always blow from cold to warm regions.

questions.question: Which Indian state is divided into Majha, Doaba and Malwa regions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Punjab**__.

__
 
• **Punjab** is a state in the northwest region of India and is one of the most prosperous states.

 
 
• The name Punjab is made of two words Punj (Five) + Aab (Water) i.e. land of five rivers.
 
• These five rivers of Punjab are **Sutlej, Beas, Ravi, Chenab, and Jhelum**. Only Sutlej, Ravi and Beas rivers flow in today’s Punjab.
 
• The other two rivers are now in the state of Punjab, situated in Pakistan.
 
• **The Punjab State is divided into three regions: Majha, Doaba and Malwa**__.

questions.question: The Kumaon Himalayas lie between which two rivers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Satluj-Kali.**__

__
 
• **Kumaun Himalayas, a west-central section of the Himalayas in northern India, extending 200 miles (320 km) from the Sutlej River east to the Kali River**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/26abd826175b37ca4d09142150568c562caf4dc9745db63d8da211d7cc77bfec.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ebdf6fb9f00783107262da248f34012aa601f83706341127942dd6ed42e5d0fe.png] 

 
• The divisions of the Himalayas that have been demarcated by the river valleys are:
 
 
• The part of the Himalayas lying between the **rivers Indus and Satluj is known as Punjab Himalayas**.
 
• **The part of the Himalayas lying between the rivers Kali and Teesta is known as Nepal Himalayas**.
 
• The part of the Himalayas lying between the rivers **Teesta and Dihang is known as Assam Himalayas**.
 
• The part of the Himalayas lying between the rivers **Satluj and Kali is known as Kumaon Himalayas**.
 
 
 
• The main Himalayan river systems are those of the Indus and the Ganga-Brahmaputra-Meghna system.
 
• The Indus, which is one of the great rivers of the world, rises near Mansarovar in Tibet and flows through India, and thereafter through Pakistan, and finally falls in the Arabian Sea near Karachi.
 
• The Brahmaputra marks the easternmost boundary of the Himalayas. Beyond the Dihang gorge, the Himalayas bend sharply to the south and spread along the eastern boundary of India.
 
• **To the south of the main Himalayas lies the Pir Panjal Range** at an average height of 5,000 meters (16,000 ft).
 
• From Gulmarg, in the northwest, it follows the southern rim of the Kashmir valley to the Banihal Pass.
 
• Here the **Pir Panjal meets the ridgeline that separates the Kashmir valley from the Warvan Valley**.

 __

questions.question: Which is the waterbody that separates Andaman Islands and Nicobar Islands?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Ten Degree Channel.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Ten Degree Channel is situated between the** Andaman Islands to the north and the Nicobar Islands to the south i**n the Bay of Bengal.
 
• The channel is approximately **150 kilometers wide** at its narrowest point.
 
• The channel plays a **crucial role in maritime navigation**, connecting the Bay of Bengal to the Andaman Sea.
 
• The Ten Degree Channel is a major** trade route** for goods traveling from the** South China Sea and Pacific to the Indian Ocean.**
 
• **Barren Island**, located in the Andaman Islands, is home to** Asia's only active volcano.**
 
• The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are home to 96 wildlife sanctuaries and one biosphere reserve.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The Nine Degree Channel separates the **Laccadive Islands** to the** west** from the **Malabar Coast** of India to the** east.**
 
• The Eleven Degree Channel lies **south of the Nicobar Islands**, separating them from the **Indonesian islands.**
 
• The Eight Degree Channel is situated between the** Lakshadweep Islands** to the north and the **Maldives** to the south.
 
• The **Great Nicobar Biosphere Reserve** is the only biosphere reserve in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
 
• The reserve includes **Galathea National Park and Campbell Bay National Park**.
 
• It was added to** UNESCO's Man and Biosphere Programme in 2013** to promote sustainable development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Man and the Biosphere (MAB) Programme** is a scientific program by UNESCO that aims to improve the **relationship between people and the environment**. 
 
• The program was** launched in 1971** and uses a combination of natural and social sciences to achieve its goals.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the Deccan Plateau is NOT correct?

options.text: The Deccan Plateau is higher in the west and slopes gently eastwards.
The Deccan Plateau is a triangular landmass.
An extension of the Plateau is also visible in the northeast.
The Satpura range flanks its broad base in the west.

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is 'The Satpura range flanks its broad base in the west'**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Deccan Plateau:**

 
 
• The Deccan Plateau is a large plateau located in southern India, characterized by its high altitude and rich volcanic soil, which supports diverse flora and fauna.
 
• This plateau is primarily a segment of the ancient Gondwanaland and includes parts of eight Indian states, stretching from the Satpura Range in the north to the Southern Indian ranges of the Eastern and Western Ghats.
 
• The plateau covers approximately 500,000 square kilometers, making it one of the largest plateaus in the world.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Features:**
 
 
• The Deccan Plateau is higher in the west and slopes gently eastwards, a characteristic that influences the flow of many rivers originating in the west and draining eastwards into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• This eastward slope is due to tectonic activity and the ancient geological processes that have shaped the land over millions of years.
 
• It forms a roughly triangular landmass, bounded by the Satpura and Vindhya Ranges to the north, the Eastern Ghats to the east, and the Western Ghats to the west.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Extension to the Northeast:**

 
 
• An extension of the Deccan Plateau is also visible in the northeast, where it merges into the Chota Nagpur Plateau. This area, rich in minerals, is crucial for India's mining industry.
 
 
 
• **Incorrect Statement about the Satpura Range:**
 
 
• The Satpura range does not flank the Deccan Plateau’s broad base in the west. Instead, it is situated to the north of the plateau and runs parallel to the Vindhya Range. Together, they demarcate the boundary between the Indo-Gangetic plains and the Deccan Plateau.
 
• The Western Ghats, a continuous range running parallel to the western coast of India, is the range that borders the Deccan Plateau on the west.
 
 
 
• **Western and Eastern Ghats:**
 
 
• The Western Ghats are known for their biodiversity and are a UNESCO World Heritage site. They rise steeply from the west coast and descend gently towards the plateau.
 
• The Eastern Ghats are a series of discontinuous hills and mountains that run along India's eastern coast. These ranges are lower in elevation compared to the Western Ghats and are less continuous.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d92ab55e5bacec835f345037d88d79a3f0e4b0c49874a3df43a4b2d7a5afe165.png]

questions.question: ________ zone is generally defined as an environment with moderate rainfall throughout the year or parts of the year, with sporadic dry, mild to hot summers and cool to cold winters.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Temperate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Temperate Zone**

 
 
• Between the** tropics and the polar regions** is where the t**emperate zone primarily exists**.
 
• There are typically **four distinct seasons**, with a **vast variation in temperatures and precipitation**.
 
• It is generally defined as an e**nvironment with moderate rainfall throughout the year or parts of the year, with sporadic dry, mild to hot summers and cool to cold winters**. 
 
• The** continental United States, the majority of Canada and Europe, Central Asia, southern South America, and southern Australia** are among the areas that are exclusively covered in the **temperate zone**.
 
• The average temperature of the temperate zone lies between zero and 20°C.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tropical Zone**

 
 
• The areas of the** planet closest to the equator and between the Tropics of Cancer in the north and Capricorn in the south are known as tropical regions**.
 
• The average temperature in the tropics ranges from **25 to 28 degrees Celsius (77 to 82 degrees Fahrenheit)**.
 
 
 
• **Dry Zone**
 
 
• The** sub-humid regions of the nation that receive 75 cm to 100 cm of rainfall **(and hence have moisture deficiency for two-thirds of the year) and the** semi-arid regions that receive 30 cm to 75 cm of rainfall are considered dry-land zones**.
 
 
 
• **Continental Zone**
 
 
• The region with the** largest geographic scope is known as the Continental Zone (CON)**, which also encompasses portions of the** lower hills on the ALS border as well as the plains and lowlands of Central and Eastern Europe and the Balkans**.
 
• The weather is continental, with** wide annual temperature variations and heavy summertime precipitation**.

questions.question: The Himalayas' outermost range is called __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option __Shivalik__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Shivalik range

 
 
• ​The Shivalik Range, also known as the outer Himalayas, is the outermost range of the Himalayas. 
 
• It features a series of parallel or converging ranges separated by deep valleys, creating a highly dissected topography. 
 
• The Shivaliks run for 2,400 km from the Potwar Plateau to the Brahmaputra valley, with altitudes ranging from 600 to 1500 meters. 
 
• The southern slopes are steep, while the northern slopes are gentler. 
 
• The range is primarily located in India, Nepal, and Bhutan, with parts extending into Tibet, Pakistan, Afghanistan, and Central Asia.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Dhauladhar Range
 
 
• Part of the Lesser Himalayas, located in Himachal Pradesh, India.
 
• Known for its rugged terrain and snow-covered peaks.
 
 
 
• Pir Panjal Range
 
 
• Part of the Outer Himalayas (or Lower Himalayas).
 
• Stretches across Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, and northern Pakistan.
 
• Famous passes include Banihal Pass and Pir Panjal Pass.
 
• The Jammu-Srinagar railway line passes through this range via the Pir Panjal Tunnel, one of the longest tunnels in India.
 
 
 
• Kanchenjunga
 
 
• The third-highest peak in the world, with an elevation of 8,586 meters (28,169 feet).
 
• Located on the border of Sikkim (India) and Nepal.
 
• Revered by locals and considered sacred.
 
• Known for its stunning beauty and challenging climbing routes.

questions.question: Fotu La, the Great Mountain Pass, at an altitude of 4108 m above sea level, is the highest point of which Indian state/UT?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jammu and Kashmir**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fotu La **

 
 
• In the** Zanskar mountain ranges of the Indian UT of Ladakh, Fotu La** is a high mountain pass on the **Srinagar-Leh road**.
 
• Fotu La pass, which rises to a** height of 4,108 metres (13,478 feet)**, is the highest point on the road beyond the well-known **Zoji La**. 
 
• It is one of the two significant mountains that passes **between Kargil and Leh**, the another one is Namik La. 
 
• A **Prasar Bharti television relay station** serving the surrounding town of Lamayuru is located at the top of the pass.
 
• You will pass through **lunar-like landscapes on your way to the Fotu La Pass**, i.e., landscapes similar to what you might have seen in moon photos.
 
• Driving across the pass is a lovely ride where you can stop to take in the** breathtaking scenery of the snow-covered mountain ranges**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Zoji La**

 
 
• It is an a**nother high mountain pass** that can be found in India, in the **Ladakh region of the Himalayas**.
 
• It is the pass, which connects **Ladakh and Kashmir**, and is located **9 kilometres from Sonmarg and is approximately 3528 metres (11, 649 feet)** above sea level.
 
• After Fotu La, this pass is regarded as the **highest on the Srinagar–Leh National Highway**.

questions.question: In which region of India are Kotli Dun and Patli Dun located?

options.text: Between greater Himalayas and the Shiwaliks
Between lesser Himalayas and Trans Himalayas
Between eastern Himalayas and the Shiwaliks
Between lesser Himalayas and the Shiwaliks

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Between the **____**lesser Himalayas and the Shiwaliks**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Duns **

 
 
• Between the **Shiwaliks and the Lesser Himalayas, there are longitudinal valleys called "Duns."**
 
• The word **"dun" is used locally to refer to a valley, especially an open valley in the Sivalik Mountains or between the Sivalik Mountains and higher Himalayan foothills**.
 
• In **Himachal**, these valleys are known by the **names Patli Dun, Kotli Dun, and Pinjore Dun**.
 
• Between the lesser Himalayas and Shivalik, there are longitudinal valleys that are referred to as** "duns" in the west and "duars" in the east**. 
 
• Unlike normal river valleys, **duns are formed structurally and are covered in rocks and gravel that were eroded from the Shiwalik uplands and the Himalayas**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Longitudinal Valley**

 
 
• An elongated valley known as a l**ongitudinal valley is one that is situated between two nearly parallel mountain ranges in geologically young fold mountains like the Alps, Carpathians, Andes, or the highlands of Central Asia**.
 
• They are frequently used by and **shaped by a later stream**.
 
• When the **Indian plate and the Eurasian plate interacted as a result of folding**, longitudinal valleys known as **dunes** were formed.
 
• They are formed between** Shivalik and the lesser Himalayas**.
 
• The H**imalayan rivers that flow down into the valleys deposit coarse alluvium** there.

questions.question: The Deccan Plateau is a _________landmass that lies to the south of the river Narmada.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**triangular**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Deccan Plateau is a **triangular** landmass that lies to the south of the river Narmada.
 
• It is one of the largest plateaus in India, covering an area of about 1.9 million square kilometers.
 
• The plateau is bounded by the Eastern Ghats and the Western Ghats, which converge at the southern tip of India.
 
• The Deccan Plateau is known for its rich mineral resources and diverse ecosystems.
 
• The region is characterized by its elevated terrain, with an average elevation ranging from 100 meters to 1,000 meters above sea level.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Deccan Plateau extends over eight Indian states, including Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and parts of Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh.
 
• It is rich in volcanic soils, which are beneficial for agriculture, particularly for growing cotton and other crops.
 
• The region has a significant historical and cultural heritage, with many ancient temples, forts, and monuments.
 
• The plateau is also home to several major rivers, including the Godavari, Krishna, and Kaveri, which are vital for irrigation and water supply in the region.
 
• The climate of the Deccan Plateau varies from arid and semi-arid in the northwest to more humid conditions in the southeast.

questions.question: Which mountain range covers a distance of about 1500 miles (2400 km) and passes through India, Pakistan, Afghanistan, China, Bhutan, and Nepal?
